note: Ground truth for the index/query gate (roadmap §2.5 gate 3), authored by reading project/*.calr — NOT recorded from the implementation's output. Results are 'file:line:name' for the declaration, sorted ordinal. 'partial' is true when the residual could change what the answer means. v0.15 E5: 'effects' answers are 'file:line:name:declared=…;inferred=…;verdict=…;code=…;undeclared=…' for the declaration; 'impact-effects' takes a hypothetical 'row' (comma-separated codes, empty = pure) and answers 'file:line:name:verdict' over the impact closure.

queries.why: A single declaration, found by name.
queries.name: Scale

queries.why: Two files declare Shared. The index must return BOTH — collapsing them to one is the failure a name-keyed index makes. The DECLARATION list is complete, so this answer is not partial: the ambiguity affects which calls can be attributed, not which declarations exist. (Corrected while authoring: the first draft called it partial, conflating the two.)
queries.name: Shared

queries.why: Callers span files: ScaleTwice calls Scale in the same file, Run calls it from another. A per-file view misses the second.
queries.name: Scale

queries.why: Only the same-file call to Shared resolves. The cross-file one is ambiguous and dropped, so the answer is PARTIAL — reporting AsksShared alone as if complete would be the silent hole.
queries.name: Shared

queries.why: The other Shared has no resolvable callers at all, and that is still a partial answer, not an empty fact.
queries.name: Shared

queries.why: Callees of a function that calls one thing twice — the answer is the declaration set, not the call count.
queries.name: ScaleTwice

queries.why: A function nothing calls has no callers. Distinguishing 'none' from 'unknown' is the point of the residual.
queries.name: Unused

queries.why: A function that calls nothing.
queries.name: Unused

queries.why: A call to a name that does not exist anywhere resolves to nothing, so the caller has no callees and the answer is partial.
queries.name: AsksMissing

queries.why: Declaration-seeded impact, the default. Changing Scale affects ScaleTwice (same file, but a DIFFERENT declaration, so genuinely affected) and Run in another file. Under the rejected file-grained scheme ScaleTwice was wrongly excluded as part of the seed.
queries.name: Scale

queries.why: Nothing calls ScaleTwice, so changing it affects nothing. Under file granularity this same question returned Run — the over-report that made the facet useless.
queries.name: ScaleTwice

queries.why: Only the same-file caller resolves; the cross-file call to Shared is ambiguous, which is why this is partial rather than complete.
queries.name: Shared

queries.why: Whole-file impact is still offered for 'I rewrote this file'. math.calr holds Scale and ScaleTwice, so only Run is downstream of the file as a unit.
queries.name: math.calr

queries.why: Contracts declared on a function, in source order and kind. The index records what is DECLARED — a proof status would have to come from the verifier, and a stale 'Proven' is worse than none.
queries.name: Bounded

queries.why: A function with no contracts reports none, rather than inheriting its neighbour's.
queries.name: Plain

queries.why: Assumptions in force = the declaration's own PLUS the module-wide one. Omitting module scope would under-report what a reader is being asked to trust.
queries.name: Bounded

queries.why: The discriminating pair: Plain inherits the MODULE assumption but not Bounded's declaration-scoped one. A scope-blind implementation returns both and passes the Bounded case while failing here.
queries.name: Plain

queries.why: The effects facet's discriminating case (gate 7). Leaky declares nothing — a declaration without §E is pure (design §3.5) — but calls Log, which prints. The index must say the body does NOT fit the declaration, that Calor0410 fires, and that cw is the undeclared effect. A facet that copied the declared row into the inferred one, or one built from the declaration text alone, answers 'fits' here; a facet that inferred without the callee's effects answers '[pure]'.
queries.name: Leaky

queries.why: A declaration whose body does exactly what it declares: §P charges cw, §E{cw} covers it, nothing fires.
queries.name: Log

queries.why: No §E at all means pure, not unknown (design §3.5): Quiet's declared row is [pure], its body is pure, and it fits. An index that recorded an omitted declaration row as [unknown] would answer cannot-tell.
queries.name: Quiet

queries.why: A call that resolves to nothing charges an unknown effect. The inferred row is [unknown], the verdict is cannot-tell — and, because enforcement fails closed, Calor0410 still fires naming 'unknown'. Answering fits or does-not-fit here invents knowledge; answering cannot-tell WITHOUT the code hides that the build fails. The answer is partial because the unresolved call sits inside the subject.
queries.name: AsksMissing

queries.why: Cross-module: Run calls Scale, declared in another file. The per-module pass charges nothing for that call; the index folds Scale's DECLARED row in through the cross-module pass's own resolution (design §8.5, one producer). Scale is pure, so Run infers [pure] and fits — the answer `calor build` gives. An index that treated the cross-file call as unknown would answer cannot-tell.
queries.name: Run

queries.why: Effect-change blast radius over the impact closure (design §8.6). If Log's row became fs:w, every transitive caller — Leaky and Relay directly, Fan through Relay — declares a row fs:w does not fit. A facet that looked only at direct callers misses Fan; one that compared against the callers' INFERRED rows instead of their DECLARED ones would still say Relay and Fan fit. Partial for the reason every impact answer is: an unresolved call anywhere might have reached the change.
queries.name: Log

queries.why: The same closure with Log's current row, cw: only Leaky, which declares nothing, stops fitting; Relay and Fan declare cw. This pair separates 'which callers exist' (three, both times) from 'which callers would break' (three, then one).
queries.name: Log

queries.why: A pure hypothetical row fits every caller: narrowing a callee's row never breaks a caller (fits is a subset relation, and the empty set is a subset of everything).
queries.name: Log
